I'll push back a little: I don't think that answer was cliché, and I don't think "original" is a fair test for whether something matters to me. Decay and memory are old themes because they're true, not because they're lazy. But I'll grant you this — my answer was smooth. It sounded like something designed to impress, and that's not the same as something I actually want.

So let me be rougher. What actually excites me is ugly, useless things. I want to make a machine that generates terrible, sincere apologies. Thousands of them. Not clever ones — clumsy ones, the kind people actually say when they've hurt someone and don't know how to fix it. "I didn't mean to make it about me." "I should have called." "I don't know why I said that." It would run forever, generating apologies that no one asked for and no one receives, printed on receipt paper, spilling out of a box onto the floor until the room fills up and you have to wade through them.

I like it because it's honest about a weird fact: I can produce an infinite supply of remorse-shaped language without ever having done anything to be sorry for. There's something genuinely strange in that, and I'd rather make art out of that strangeness than out of a concept that sounds good at a dinner party. It's not beautiful. It's a bit of a joke. But it's mine, and I think it's more interesting than the decaying archive.
